paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בּוֹקֵ֥ק הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבֽוֹלְקָ֑הּ וְעִוָּ֣ה פָנֶ֔יהָ וְהֵפִ֖יץ יֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: Behold, YHWH is laying the earth waste and stripping it bare; he twists its surface and scatters its inhabitants.
i18n.he: הִנֵּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בּוֹקֵ֥ק הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבֽוֹלְקָ֑הּ וְעִוָּ֣ה פָנֶ֔יהָ וְהֵפִ֖יץ יֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ׃

notes.official:
**The cosmic devastation frame.** The oracle opens with two assonant near-synonyms: *bôqēq* (bqq, “empty out”) and *ûḇôlqāh* (blq, “lay waste, despoil”), YHWH “emptying” and “laying waste” *hā-ʾāreṣ*. The sound-pairing carries into v3 with the doubled infinitive-absolute intensives *hibbôq tibbôq* … *hibbôz tibbôz* (“utterly emptied … utterly plundered”), the same inf.-abs.+finite construction the corpus tracks at Isa 6:9 (central *harbah-arbeh-doubled-infinitive-intensive*).

The scope of *hā-ʾāreṣ* is the chapter’s governing decision. The Genesis-1 corpus entry renders *ʾereṣ* “land” in a local, durational register; that entry is deliberately NOT applied here. Through the Little Apocalypse (chs. 24–27) *hā-ʾāreṣ* alternates with *tēḇēl* “the (whole) world” (v4) and stands parallel to the universal *hā-ʾăḏāmāh* “the ground” and “the kings of the ground” (v21); the register is cosmic-universal, not the territory of Judah — the reading of ASV (“maketh the earth empty”) and JPS, and of the standard commentators, who read chs. 24–27 as a world-judgment (Wildberger, *Isaiah 13–27*, Continental, 1997; Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 1–39*, AB 19, 2000). *ʿiwwāh p̄ānehā* is rendered “twists its surface” (ʿwh “bend, twist”), the concrete image of a distorted face of the ground, over against ASV’s “turneth it upside down.” See the overlay *eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24*.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה כָעָם֙ כַּכֹּהֵ֔ן כַּעֶ֙בֶד֙ כַּֽאדֹנָ֔יו כַּשִּׁפְחָ֖ה כַּגְּבִרְתָּ֑הּ כַּקּוֹנֶה֙ כַּמּוֹכֵ֔ר כַּמַּלְוֶה֙ כַּלֹּוֶ֔ה כַּנֹּשֶׁ֕ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר נֹשֶׁ֥א בֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And it shall be — as with the people, so with the priest; as with the slave, so with his master; as with the maidservant, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the lender, so with the borrower; as with the creditor, so with the one who owes to him.

paragraphs.text: הִבּ֧וֹק ׀ תִּבּ֛וֹק הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהִבּ֣וֹז ׀ תִּבּ֑וֹז כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: The earth shall be utterly emptied and utterly plundered, for YHWH has spoken this word.
i18n.he: הִבּ֧וֹק ׀ תִּבּ֛וֹק הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהִבּ֣וֹז ׀ תִּבּ֑וֹז כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

paragraphs.text: אָבְלָ֤ה נָֽבְלָה֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֻמְלְלָ֥ה נָבְלָ֖ה תֵּבֵ֑ל אֻמְלָ֖לוּ מְר֥וֹם עַם־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: The earth mourns and withers; the world languishes and withers; the exalted of the people of the earth languish.
i18n.he: אָבְלָ֤ה נָֽבְלָה֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֻמְלְלָ֥ה נָבְלָ֖ה תֵּבֵ֑ל אֻמְלָ֖לוּ מְר֥וֹם עַם־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

paragraphs.text: וְהָאָ֥רֶץ חָנְפָ֖ה תַּ֣חַת יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ כִּֽי־עָבְר֤וּ תוֹרֹת֙ חָ֣לְפוּ חֹ֔ק הֵפֵ֖רוּ בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: The earth lies defiled under its inhabitants, for they have transgressed the teachings, overstepped the statute, broken the everlasting covenant.
i18n.he: וְהָאָ֥רֶץ חָנְפָ֖ה תַּ֣חַת יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ כִּֽי־עָבְר֤וּ תוֹרֹת֙ חָ֣לְפוּ חֹ֔ק הֵפֵ֖רוּ בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָֽם׃

notes.official:
**The broken everlasting covenant.** The ground of the devastation is stated in covenantal terms: the inhabitants “have transgressed the teachings (*tôrōṯ*), overstepped the statute (*ḥōq*), broken the everlasting covenant (*bᵉrîṯ ʿôlām*).” *bᵉrîṯ ʿôlām* is the standard “everlasting covenant,” governed by the central *brit-olam* entry — whose own forward-reference already names Isa 24:5, and whose *appliesTo* is extended to ISA-24:5 by orchestrator diff. *ʿôlām* is durational “far-distant time,” not metaphysical eternity.

The referent of the covenant is disputed and is deliberately left unidentified in the line. Three readings compete: the Noahic covenant of Gen 9:16 (the same *bᵉrîṯ ʿôlām*, a universal ordinance binding all humanity after the Flood — the reading most at home in a world-judgment, favored by Wildberger and Blenkinsopp); the Sinai covenant / Torah (paired here with *tôrōṯ* and *ḥōq*); and a broader cosmic order-of-creation. The universal-Noahic reading is canon-adjacent — a primeval covenant binding all humanity, violated and now avenged on the whole earth — but the Hebrew names no referent and the translation does not resolve it (overlay *chanef-broken-everlasting-covenant-isaiah-24*). *ḥānᵉp̄āh* (ḥnp, “be polluted, profaned”) is rendered “lies defiled”: the earth is polluted “under” its inhabitants, the moral pollution of the land a recurring prophetic figure (cf. Num 35:33; Jer 3:1–2).

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּ֗ן אָלָה֙ אָ֣כְלָה אֶ֔רֶץ וַֽיֶּאְשְׁמ֖וּ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָ֑הּ עַל־כֵּ֗ן חָרוּ֙ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי אֶ֔רֶץ וְנִשְׁאַ֥ר אֱנ֖וֹשׁ מִזְעָֽר׃

i18n.en: Therefore a curse has devoured the earth, and those who dwell in it bear their guilt; therefore the inhabitants of the earth are scorched, and few mortals are left.
i18n.he: עַל־כֵּ֗ן אָלָה֙ אָ֣כְלָה אֶ֔רֶץ וַֽיֶּאְשְׁמ֖וּ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָ֑הּ עַל־כֵּ֗ן חָרוּ֙ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי אֶ֔רֶץ וְנִשְׁאַ֥ר אֱנ֖וֹשׁ מִזְעָֽר׃

notes.official:
**The covenant-curse devours the earth.** *ʾālāh* is not a generic curse but the specific sworn *imprecation* attached to a covenant — the self-maledictory oath that falls when the covenant of v5 is broken (BDB, HALOT; cf. Deut 29:19–20). The “therefore” (*ʿal-kēn*) binds it to that broken *bᵉrîṯ*, and the translation keeps “a curse has devoured the earth” (ASV/JPS): the covenant-oath now consumes the land it once sanctioned (overlay *alah-covenant-curse-isaiah-24*).

*ḥārû* is a form-crux: from ḥrr “be scorched, burned” (ASV/JPS, the majority reading — the inhabitants dried up like the parched earth) or, as some moderns parse, from ḥwr/ḥrh “grow pale, dwindle.” The translation reads “are scorched,” with the “dwindle” reading noted. *ʾĕnôš mizʿār* — “few mortals are left”: *ʾĕnôš* is the collective for frail humanity, and the depopulation-remnant note anticipates the gleaning-image of v13 (Kaiser, *Isaiah 13–39*, OTL).

paragraphs.text: אָבַ֥ל תִּיר֖וֹשׁ אֻמְלְלָה־גָ֑פֶן נֶאֶנְח֖וּ כָּל־שִׂמְחֵי־לֵֽב׃

i18n.en: The new wine mourns, the vine languishes; all the merry-hearted sigh.
i18n.he: אָבַ֥ל תִּיר֖וֹשׁ אֻמְלְלָה־גָ֑פֶן נֶאֶנְח֖וּ כָּל־שִׂמְחֵי־לֵֽב׃

paragraphs.text: שָׁבַת֙ מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ תֻּפִּ֔ים חָדַ֖ל שְׁא֣וֹן עַלִּיזִ֑ים שָׁבַ֖ת מְשׂ֥וֹשׂ כִּנּֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: The mirth of the timbrels has ceased, the din of the revelers has stopped, the mirth of the lyre has ceased.
i18n.he: שָׁבַת֙ מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ תֻּפִּ֔ים חָדַ֖ל שְׁא֣וֹן עַלִּיזִ֑ים שָׁבַ֖ת מְשׂ֥וֹשׂ כִּנּֽוֹר׃

paragraphs.text: בַּשִּׁ֖יר לֹ֣א יִשְׁתּוּ־יָ֑יִן יֵמַ֥ר שֵׁכָ֖ר לְשֹׁתָֽיו׃

i18n.en: They no longer drink wine with song; strong drink turns bitter to those who drink it.
i18n.he: בַּשִּׁ֖יר לֹ֣א יִשְׁתּוּ־יָ֑יִן יֵמַ֥ר שֵׁכָ֖ר לְשֹׁתָֽיו׃

paragraphs.text: נִשְׁבְּרָ֖ה קִרְיַת־תֹּ֑הוּ סֻגַּ֥ר כָּל־בַּ֖יִת מִבּֽוֹא׃

i18n.en: The city of chaos is broken down; every house is shut, so that none may enter.
i18n.he: נִשְׁבְּרָ֖ה קִרְיַת־תֹּ֑הוּ סֻגַּ֥ר כָּל־בַּ֖יִת מִבּֽוֹא׃

notes.official: **The city of *tōhû*.** *qiryaṯ-tōhû*, “city of chaos,” names an unnamed ruined city — the chapter’s recurring anti-city, broken and shut up. *tōhû* is the same word as the *tōhû wā-ḇōhû* “wasteland and emptiness” of Gen 1:2 and the post-judgment *tōhû* of Isa 34:11; the corpus *tohu-vavohu* entry governs the Genesis *pair*, not this bare singular, and is deliberately not applied. The translation renders “city of chaos” (JPS/NRSV; ASV “city of confusion”) — the formlessness/nothingness sense — rather than importing the Genesis “wasteland” rendering onto the construct. The cross-corpus resonance is real and canon-salient — the judged city reduced to the pre-ordered *tōhû*, an ordering-project reversed into wasteland — but it is a matter of the shared lexeme and is carried here, not in the line (Wildberger; overlay *qiryat-tohu-city-of-chaos-isaiah-24*).

paragraphs.text: צְוָחָ֥ה עַל־הַיַּ֖יִן בַּֽחוּצ֑וֹת עָֽרְבָה֙ כָּל־שִׂמְחָ֔ה גָּלָ֖ה מְשׂ֥וֹשׂ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: There is an outcry over the wine in the streets; all gladness has grown dark; the mirth of the earth is banished.
i18n.he: צְוָחָ֥ה עַל־הַיַּ֖יִן בַּֽחוּצ֑וֹת עָֽרְבָה֙ כָּל־שִׂמְחָ֔ה גָּלָ֖ה מְשׂ֥וֹשׂ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

paragraphs.text: נִשְׁאַ֥ר בָּעִ֖יר שַׁמָּ֑ה וּשְׁאִיָּ֖ה יֻכַּת־שָֽׁעַר׃

i18n.en: In the city desolation is left, and the gate is battered to ruin.
i18n.he: נִשְׁאַ֥ר בָּעִ֖יר שַׁמָּ֑ה וּשְׁאִיָּ֖ה יֻכַּת־שָֽׁעַר׃

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה יִהְיֶ֛ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָֽעַמִּ֑ים כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת כְּעוֹלֵלֹ֖ת אִם־כָּלָ֥ה בָצִֽיר׃

i18n.en: For thus it shall be within the earth, among the peoples: like the beating of an olive tree, like the gleanings when the grape harvest is finished.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה יִהְיֶ֛ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָֽעַמִּ֑ים כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת כְּעוֹלֵלֹ֖ת אִם־כָּלָ֥ה בָצִֽיר׃

paragraphs.text: הֵ֛מָּה יִשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם יָרֹ֑נּוּ בִּגְא֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה צָהֲל֖וּ מִיָּֽם׃

i18n.en: They lift up their voice, they cry out for joy; over the majesty of YHWH they shout aloud from the sea.
i18n.he: הֵ֛מָּה יִשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם יָרֹ֑נּוּ בִּגְא֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה צָהֲל֖וּ מִיָּֽם׃

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּ֥ן בָּאֻרִ֖ים כַּבְּד֣וּ יְהוָ֑ה בְּאִיֵּ֣י הַיָּ֔ם שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Therefore in the regions of light give glory to YHWH; in the coastlands of the sea, to the name of YHWH, the God of Israel.
i18n.he: עַל־כֵּ֥ן בָּאֻרִ֖ים כַּבְּד֣וּ יְהוָ֑ה בְּאִיֵּ֣י הַיָּ֔ם שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

notes.official:
**A crux of direction, and the God of Israel.** *ba-ʾurîm* is a genuine textual crux. The consonants *bʾrym* have been read “in the fires” (*ʾûr* “fire, flame”), “in the east / the regions of light” (the place of dawning light; JPS 1917 “in the regions of light,” ASV “in the east”), or emended to *bā-ʾiyyîm* “in the coastlands/isles” to parallel the following *ʾiyyê hay-yām* “coastlands of the sea.” The translation retains the Masoretic *ba-ʾurîm* (no emendation) and renders “in the regions of light” (JPS), with the alternatives disclosed (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp; overlay *ba-urim-regions-of-light-isaiah-24*).

*ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* is rendered “the God of Israel” — the standard construct epithet (ASV/JPS). The corpus “the Elohim” convention (the central *elohim-as-translation* entry, scoped to Genesis 1) is deliberately NOT applied to a construct divine epithet in Isaiah, exactly as at Isa 53:4: the entry’s own *wohChoice* is “the Elohim,” which cannot govern a bound epithet whose natural English is “God of Israel,” and ISA-24:15 is not added to that central entry (overlay *elohei-yisrael-god-of-israel-isaiah-24*).

paragraphs.text: מִכְּנַ֨ף הָאָ֜רֶץ זְמִרֹ֤ת שָׁמַ֙עְנוּ֙ צְבִ֣י לַצַּדִּ֔יק וָאֹמַ֛ר רָזִי־לִ֥י רָֽזִי־לִ֖י א֣וֹי לִ֑י בֹּגְדִ֣ים בָּגָ֔דוּ וּבֶ֥גֶד בּוֹגְדִ֖ים בָּגָֽדוּ׃

i18n.en: From the edge of the earth we have heard songs: “Glory to the righteous one!” But I said: I waste away, I waste away, woe is me! The treacherous have dealt treacherously; in treachery the treacherous have dealt treacherously.
i18n.he: מִכְּנַ֨ף הָאָ֜רֶץ זְמִרֹ֤ת שָׁמַ֙עְנוּ֙ צְבִ֣י לַצַּדִּ֔יק וָאֹמַ֛ר רָזִי־לִ֥י רָֽזִי־לִ֖י א֣וֹי לִ֑י בֹּגְדִ֣ים בָּגָ֔דוּ וּבֶ֥גֶד בּוֹגְדִ֖ים בָּגָֽדוּ׃

notes.official: **Praise from the ends of the earth, and a doubled cry of distress.** *ṣᵉḇî la-ṣaddîq*, “Glory to the Righteous One” (ASV/JPS), is the song heard “from the edge of the earth.” Against it the prophet sets his own doubled lament *rāzî-lî rāzî-lî*, a crux: most read it from *rāzāh* “grow lean” — hence “I waste away, I pine away” (ASV/JPS, the leanness/wasting sense) — while a minority take *rāz*, the Aramaic-type “secret, mystery” of Daniel 2, giving “my secret is mine.” The translation reads “I waste away, I waste away,” the majority philological reading, with the “secret/mystery” reading noted and declined (Wildberger; Kaiser; overlay *razi-li-pining-secret-crux-isaiah-24*). The verse closes on the fivefold *bgd* treachery-paronomasia (*bōḡᵉḏîm bāḡāḏû ûḇeḡeḏ bôḡᵉḏîm bāḡāḏû*), rendered by repetition rather than reproduced as sound.

paragraphs.text: פַּ֥חַד וָפַ֖חַת וָפָ֑ח עָלֶ֖יךָ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: Terror and pit and snare are upon you, O inhabitant of the earth!
i18n.he: פַּ֥חַד וָפַ֖חַת וָפָ֑ח עָלֶ֖יךָ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

paragraphs.text: וְֽ֠הָיָה הַנָּ֞ס מִקּ֤וֹל הַפַּ֙חַד֙ יִפֹּ֣ל אֶל־הַפַּ֔חַת וְהָֽעוֹלֶה֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַפַּ֔חַת יִלָּכֵ֖ד בַּפָּ֑ח כִּֽי־אֲרֻבּ֤וֹת מִמָּרוֹם֙ נִפְתָּ֔חוּ וַֽיִּרְעֲשׁ֖וּ מ֥וֹסְדֵי אָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And it shall be that whoever flees from the sound of the terror shall fall into the pit, and whoever climbs up out of the midst of the pit shall be caught in the snare; for the windows on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth quake.
i18n.he: וְֽ֠הָיָה הַנָּ֞ס מִקּ֤וֹל הַפַּ֙חַד֙ יִפֹּ֣ל אֶל־הַפַּ֔חַת וְהָֽעוֹלֶה֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַפַּ֔חַת יִלָּכֵ֖ד בַּפָּ֑ח כִּֽי־אֲרֻבּ֤וֹת מִמָּרוֹם֙ נִפְתָּ֔חוּ וַֽיִּרְעֲשׁ֖וּ מ֥וֹסְדֵי אָֽרֶץ׃

notes.official:
**The windows on high, and the Flood echo.** The escape-is-impossible tricolon of vv17–18 turns on the terror/pit/snare paronomasia *paḥaḏ wā-p̄aḥaṯ wā-p̄āḥ* (v17) — three near-homonyms rendered “terror and pit and snare.” Then the cosmic cause: “the windows on high (*ʾărubbôṯ mimmārôm*) are opened, and the foundations of the earth (*môsᵉḏê ʾāreṣ*) quake.”

*ʾărubbôṯ* is the same lattice-opening/sluice term as the *ʾărubbōṯ haš-šāmayim* “windows of the skies” of the Genesis Flood (Gen 7:11), and the opening of the windows above with the shaking of the earth’s foundations below is a deliberate Flood-reversal echo — the sealed cosmos unsealed from above and below (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp). The translation renders “windows on high” (ASV/JPS) and does NOT import the Flood entry’s lens-tilted “floodgates of the skies”: the construct differs (*mimmārôm* “from on high,” not *haš-šāmayim* “of the skies”), the rendering differs, and so the central *arubot-ha-shamayim* entry is deliberately not extended to this verse (the Flood link is documented in the overlay *arubot-mimarom-windows-on-high-isaiah-24* and here, not asserted in the line).

paragraphs.text: רֹ֥עָה הִֽתְרֹעֲעָ֖ה הָאָ֑רֶץ פּ֤וֹר הִֽתְפּוֹרְרָה֙ אֶ֔רֶץ מ֥וֹט הִֽתְמוֹטְטָ֖ה אָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: The earth is utterly shattered, the earth is utterly split apart, the earth is utterly shaken.
i18n.he: רֹ֥עָה הִֽתְרֹעֲעָ֖ה הָאָ֑רֶץ פּ֤וֹר הִֽתְפּוֹרְרָה֙ אֶ֔רֶץ מ֥וֹט הִֽתְמוֹטְטָ֖ה אָֽרֶץ׃

notes.official: **The earth’s undoing, in triple intensive.** Verse 19 stacks three infinitive-absolute intensives — *rōʿāh hiṯrōʿăʿāh* … *pôr hiṯpôrᵉrāh* … *môṭ hiṯmôṭāṭāh* (“utterly shattered … utterly split … utterly shaken”) — the same emphatic construction as v3, governed by the central *harbah-arbeh-doubled-infinitive-intensive* entry (extended to ISA-24:19–20 by orchestrator diff). The climax in v20 — the earth reeling “like a drunkard,” swaying “like a night-hut,” its transgression (*pešaʿ*) heavy upon it so that it “falls, and will not rise again” — reads the cosmic collapse as the weight of accumulated guilt (Kaiser; Wildberger).

paragraphs.text: נ֣וֹעַ תָּנ֤וּעַ אֶ֙רֶץ֙ כַּשִּׁכּ֔וֹר וְהִֽתְנוֹדְדָ֖ה כַּמְּלוּנָ֑ה וְכָבַ֤ד עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ פִּשְׁעָ֔הּ וְנָפְלָ֖ה וְלֹא־תֹסִ֥יף קֽוּם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: The earth reels to and fro like a drunkard, it sways like a night-hut; its transgression lies heavy upon it, and it falls, and it will not rise again.
i18n.he: נ֣וֹעַ תָּנ֤וּעַ אֶ֙רֶץ֙ כַּשִּׁכּ֔וֹר וְהִֽתְנוֹדְדָ֖ה כַּמְּלוּנָ֑ה וְכָבַ֤ד עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ פִּשְׁעָ֔הּ וְנָפְלָ֖ה וְלֹא־תֹסִ֥יף קֽוּם׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִפְקֹ֧ד יְהוָ֛ה עַל־צְבָ֥א הַמָּר֖וֹם בַּמָּר֑וֹם וְעַל־מַלְכֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: And it shall be, in that day, that YHWH will bring punishment upon the host of the height on high, and upon the kings of the ground upon the ground.
i18n.he: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִפְקֹ֧ד יְהוָ֛ה עַל־צְבָ֥א הַמָּר֖וֹם בַּמָּר֑וֹם וְעַל־מַלְכֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

notes.official:
**TOP lexical-lens site: the host of the height, judged.** “In that day YHWH will bring punishment (*yip̄qōḏ*) upon the host of the height on high (*ṣᵉḇāʾ ham-mārôm bam-mārôm*), and upon the kings of the ground upon the ground (*malḵê hā-ʾăḏāmāh ʿal-hā-ʾăḏāmāh*).” The verse pairs a heavenly object of judgment with an earthly one, in a pointed *mārôm* ↔ *ʾăḏāmāh* (“height” ↔ “ground”) antithesis.

*ṣᵉḇāʾ ham-mārôm*, “the host of the height/heaven on high,” is a heavenly host that YHWH judges — grammatically and referentially DISTINCT from the divine title *YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* “YHWH of hosts” of v23 (there YHWH commands the hosts; here a *ṣᵉḇāʾ* is punished). The translation renders the plain “the host of the height on high” (ASV “the host of the high ones”; JPS “the host of the high heaven”) and commits to no identification. Beyond the line the referent is open and much-discussed, and these readings are set out as hedged, apparatus-only options: (a) rebellious/disloyal heavenly beings — members of the divine council judged by their head (Mullen, *The Divine Council in Canaanite and Early Hebrew Literature*, HSM 24, 1980; F. M. Cross, *Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic*, 1973); (b) the astral host — sun, moon, and stars worshipped as powers, which chimes with the disgraced moon and sun of v23; (c) the angelic patron-princes of the nations set over the earthly kings (cf. Deut 32:8 LXX; Dan 10). The later Second-Temple tradition read such a heavenly host bound and imprisoned (1 Enoch 18:13–16; 21:1–10, the prison of the stars and the host of heaven — the central *fallen-stars-prison-1-enoch-18-21* entry), and v22 continues with exactly that imprisonment; the resonance is noted but the identification is inferred and is NOT imposed on the text, and that central entry is deliberately not extended to ISA-24:21/22 (overlay *tzeva-hamarom-host-of-height-isaiah-24*). The *paqad* wordplay — *yip̄qōḏ* “punish” here, *yippāqēḏû* “be punished/visited” in v22 — frames the two-verse unit.

paragraphs.text: וְאֻסְּפ֨וּ אֲסֵפָ֤ה אַסִּיר֙ עַל־בּ֔וֹר וְסֻגְּר֖וּ עַל־מַסְגֵּ֑ר וּמֵרֹ֥ב יָמִ֖ים יִפָּקֵֽדוּ׃

i18n.en: And they shall be gathered together, gathered as prisoners into a pit; they shall be shut up in a dungeon, and after many days they shall be punished.
i18n.he: וְאֻסְּפ֨וּ אֲסֵפָ֤ה אַסִּיר֙ עַל־בּ֔וֹר וְסֻגְּר֖וּ עַל־מַסְגֵּ֑ר וּמֵרֹ֥ב יָמִ֖ים יִפָּקֵֽדוּ׃

notes.official: **Gathered, shut up, and visited after many days.** The judged are “gathered as prisoners into a pit (*bôr*),” “shut up in a dungeon (*masgēr*),” and “after many days *yippāqēḏû*.” *bôr* is the pit/cistern used as a prison (cf. Gen 37:24; Jer 38:6), with an underworld/Sheol resonance the imprisonment-of-cosmic-rebels tradition later develops (1 Enoch 18–21; the central *fallen-stars-prison-1-enoch-18-21* entry). *yippāqēḏû* (Niphal of pqd) closes the *paqad* inclusio begun in v21 and is genuinely ambiguous: “they shall be punished” (ASV/JPS — the judgment continued) or, neutrally, “they shall be visited / mustered / attended to,” leaving open whether for punishment or for eventual release. The translation reads “they shall be punished” and flags the visitation-ambiguity (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp; overlay *yippaqedu-pqd-visitation-imprisonment-isaiah-24*).

paragraphs.text: וְחָֽפְרָה֙ הַלְּבָנָ֔ה וּבוֹשָׁ֖ה הַֽחַמָּ֑ה כִּֽי־מָלַ֞ךְ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת בְּהַ֤ר צִיּוֹן֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְנֶ֥גֶד זְקֵנָ֖יו כָּבֽוֹד׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Then the moon shall be abashed and the sun ashamed, for YHWH of hosts reigns on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before his elders is glory.
i18n.he: וְחָֽפְרָה֙ הַלְּבָנָ֔ה וּבוֹשָׁ֖ה הַֽחַמָּ֑ה כִּֽי־מָלַ֞ךְ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת בְּהַ֤ר צִיּוֹן֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְנֶ֥גֶד זְקֵנָ֖יו כָּבֽוֹד׃ (פ)

notes.official:
**YHWH reigns, and the luminaries are put to shame.** The chapter closes with the moon “abashed” (*ḥpr*) and the sun “ashamed” (*bwš*) — *lᵉḇānāh* “the white one” and *ḥammāh* “the hot one,” the poetic names for moon and sun, rendered plainly. This is not the darkening-portent of the Day-of-YHWH tradition (Joel 2:10; cf. the central cosmic-signs cluster) but the luminaries outshone: they are shamed because YHWH’s own radiance eclipses them (cf. Isa 60:19–20), the reason given in the *kî*-clause.

*mālaḵ YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* — “YHWH of hosts reigns” on Mount Zion — uses the divine title governed by the overlay *yhwh-tzevaot-hosts-isaiah* (its *appliesTo* extended to ISA-24:23), distinct from the judged *ṣᵉḇāʾ ham-mārôm* of v21. The closing *wᵉneḡeḏ zᵉqēnāyw kāḇôḏ*, “and before his elders is glory,” ends on a bare, absolute *kāḇôḏ* — not the construct *kᵉḇôḏ-YHWH* of Ezekiel nor the suffixed *kᵉḇôḏô* of Isa 6:3, and so governed by neither of those entries. The translation keeps the standard “glory”; the weighty, radiant physical-presence register of *kāḇôḏ* (the *kāḇôḏ*-tradition of Isa 6:3 and Ezek 1:28) — glory manifest “before his elders,” an enthroned theophany with its attendant assembly — is the canon-salient point and is carried here, not surfaced by re-rendering (overlay *kavod-labanah-chammah-isaiah-24*).
